However, the Lions battled back through Erich Cronje’s second try, Chris Smith’s accurate boot and a late Kelly Mpeku score.

Rugby.title: Comebacks, fly-hacks and cornrows
Rugby.summary: Old names, new looks and some stunning scores marked the return of the Prem for another season.
Rugby.body:
At the start of pre-season, at their St Albans training ground, Brendan Venter made a speech to his Saracens squad. "I don't want to be competitive in this league," the returning director of rugby said. "I want to dominate."

Sarries were short of domination - the lead swapped hands four times in the final half hour of a blockbuster - but victory away at Leicester was a fine statement of intent. Hobbled by an injury to Olly Hartley in the first half and then reduced to 14 men by Nick Isiekwe's 20-minute red card in the second, the visitors nonetheless dug deep and silenced the baying Tigers fans with an extraordinary 40-38 win.

Rugby.title: Boks escape creating two unwanted records in Perth defeat
Rugby.summary: To score five tries and 38 points and still lose a Test match is rare, especially for a team of the calibre of world champions South Africa.
Rugby.body:
The 1999 Rugby World Cup-winning Wallabies famously lifted the Webb Ellis Cup in Cardiff having only conceded a now unthinkable one try all tournament, with the United States surprisingly the team to deny them a complete shut-out.

Back then the mantra of defence wins championships rung true, but not any more. “I remember coaching a team in Wales who went five games without conceding one try, and that’s impossible now. It is for the better of the game,” acknowledged defence coach guru Shaun Edwards earlier this year.

Rugby.title: The major caveat hanging over the Springboks' defeat in Perth
Rugby.summary: Australia deserved every second of its celebration in Perth. The Wallabies scored five tries against the world champions, led 42-17 with a quarter of an hour left...
Rugby.body:
Australia deserved every second of its celebration in Perth. The Wallabies scored five tries against the world champions, led 42-17 with a quarter of an hour left, and somehow survived the closing minutes with four players in the sin bin. Len Ikitau was outstanding, Joseph-Aukuso Sua’ali’i helped win the aerial contest, and Les Kiss’s side looked quicker and more forceful for most of the match. The 42-38 final score flatters South Africa and there can be no question that the deserving team took the spoils.

It may prove an important night for Australian rugby. A home World Cup is approaching, and this was a victory around which players and supporters can build belief. The Guardian described it as the match Australian rugby needed. One could make the case that it is the best result in Australian rugby for over a decade. But that is looking at this story from David’s perspective. For Goliath, it is but a flesh wound.

Rugby.title: Baxter wants reaction after heavy Gloucester loss
Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says hopes he will see a reaction from his side after their surprising 45-24 home loss to Gloucester.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter hopes he will see a reaction from his side after their surprising 45-24 home loss to Gloucester. Last season's beaten Prem finalists began the new season by conceding seven tries as a bout of illness went through the home camp.

It was a biggest home loss in any competition since Bordeaux hammered a struggling Exeter side 69-17 at Sandy Park in a Champions Cup fixture in January 2025 . "You've got to be really careful that you don't assume things are going quite well and actually you've got to put your foot down because it's a game of Premiership rugby and you have to work extremely hard to make good things happen," Baxter told BBC Radio Devon.

Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus insisted South Africa's unprecedented decision to unload their entire bench in the 47th minute against Australia was a reaction...
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus insisted South Africa’s unprecedented decision to unload their entire bench in the 47th minute against Australia was a reaction to events rather than a move that had been mapped out before kick-off.

The Wallabies led 24-17 at the break and stretched that advantage to 42-17 after 65 minutes. While the Springboks mounted a late fightback and closed to within four points, Erasmus said the decision to deploy all eight replacements at once was driven by the flow of the match.

The Cherry and Whites were confident winners against the Chiefs, beating the 2025-26 Prem finalists 45-24 on their own pitch for a first win at Sandy Park in 12 years.

Rugby.title: Fifteen vs Eleven! It's happened before in Test rugby
Rugby.summary: Australia's 42-38 win over the world champions Springboks was remarkable in many ways, not least for the four yellow cards received by the Wallabies
Rugby.body:
It was a game seemingly like no other, one watched in disbelief by the 54,678 present at the Optus Stadium in Perth and the millions watching on devices at home. Australia’s 42-38 win over the world champions Springboks was remarkable in many ways, not least for the four yellow cards received by the Wallabies in a chaotic seven-minute spell between the 68th and 75th minutes.

As our man on the spot, Finn Morton, reported, the Wallabies went down to 13 after yellow cards in quick succession to Harry Wilson and Ryan Lonergan, before Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and then Hunter Paisami joined them in the over-crowded sin bin.

Rugby.title: URC table: Irish sides hit 16 year low as South Africans and Scots sitting pretty
Rugby.summary: The opening round of the new BKT URC season saw a clean-sweep for South Africa and Scotland, while it was a rare winless weekend for Ireland.
Rugby.body:
The opening round of the new BKT URC season saw a clean-sweep for South Africa and Scotland, while it was a rare winless weekend for Ireland. It’s actually the first time since 2009 that all four Irish sides have lost on the first weekend of the league campaign.

In a further rarity, there were just two home wins from the eight matches, bucking the traditional trend in the competition. One of those solitary successes on home soil was recorded by the 10Bet Lions who claimed a notable scalp by beating reigning champions Leinster Rugby 27-26 in Johannesburg.

Rugby.summary: Double World Cup-winning Springbok Steven Kitshoff has asserted that South Africa could have 15 injuries at next year's World Cup and still win an unprecedented third title in a row.
Rugby.body:
Double World Cup-winning Springbok Steven Kitshoff has asserted that South Africa could have 15 injuries at next year’s World Cup and still win an unprecedented third title in a row.

A Springboks squad that had seen 13 changes from the XV that started the final Test against the All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry narrowly lost to Australia 42-38 on Sunday, almost overturning a 42-17 second-half deficit in the final 15 minutes in Perth to come within a whisker of snatching victory with the final play of the match.

Rugby.title: Chaotic ending robs Wallabies of world rankings 4-year high
Rugby.summary: When Australia led South Africa 42-17 with 17 minutes left to go, it looked for all the world that they would beat the Springboks by a big enough margin to leapfrog both Scotland and England.
Rugby.body:
When Australia led South Africa 42-17 with 17 minutes left to go, it looked for all the world that they would beat the Springboks by a big enough margin to leapfrog both Scotland and England and move up to fifth in the World Rugby Men’s Rankings.

However, the concession of four yellow cards – the most the Wallabies have ever received in a single Test – put paid to that notion, and instead they were glad to hang on to a precious 42-38 victory against the world champions.

Rugby.title: Pirates concede record 73-point haul at Coventry
Rugby.summary: Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are not as bad as their 73-40 defeat at Coventry would suggest.
Rugby.body:
Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are not as bad as their 73-40 defeat at Coventry would suggest. Pirates conceded 11 tries as they let in a club-record amount of points in a Champ fixture, four more than in their record 69-8 loss to Worcester Warriors in April 2015.

Pirates were hampered by centre Joe Elderkin being injured in the warm-up. They had fly-half Arwel Robson and replacement forward Matt Cannon yellow carded within three minutes of one another early in the second half as they conceded five tries in a 13-minute period surrounding the duo entering the sin bin.

Rugby.title: The Wallabies’ three biggest concerns ahead of All Blacks clash at Eden Park
Rugby.summary: Hunter Paisami and Len Ikitau, the trusted centre combination which first took shape under Dave Rennie, has now returned, and boy do they look better many caps later.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have done the unthinkable by putting 42 points on the Springboks in Perth; it is a statement scoreline by the now sixth-ranked Wallabies. For all the talk about officiating, downed communications, and substitution confusion, the Wallabies nevertheless found a way to score five tries and three penalty goals, all adding up to 42 points.

The Wallabies had the Springboks dead to rights with just 10 minutes left in the game, 42 points to 17, a margin of 25 points, or more than three converted tries. Anyway you cut it, the Wallabies were dominant over this heavily reshuffled Springboks side.

Rugby.summary: Saracens head coach Joe Shaw believes his team’s dramatic victory at Leicester Tigers was down to them staying cool despite the adversity they faced.
Rugby.body:
Saracens head coach Joe Shaw believes his team’s dramatic victory at Leicester Tigers was down to them staying cool despite the adversity they faced. In their opening Gallagher PREM fixture of the season, Sarries lost centre Olly Hartley to an arm injury early in proceedings and flanker Nick Isiekwe to a 20-minute red card in the second half.

Rugby.title: 'We take full accountability': Kévin Rouet laments Canada performance in La Rochelle
Rugby.summary: Canada head coach Kévin Rouet cut a frustrated figure at full-time of his team's 21-5 loss to France in La Rochelle.
Rugby.body:
Canada head coach Kévin Rouet cut a frustrated figure at full-time of his team’s 21-5 loss to France in La Rochelle. The 39-year-old watched his team struggle to make an impact against François Ratier’s team on the French west coast, as the hosts controlled the fixture from start to finish. Simply put, Canada were outclassed.

An Émilie Boulard brace, a try from Alexandra Chambon and conversions from Carla Arbez and Lina Queyroi cancelled out Lizzie Gibson’s 35th-minute try. While Gibson has seen her stock rise with four tries in three WXV Global Series fixtures this autumn, the overall performance was a stark contrast to the 26-all draw with England a week prior and their 10-try win against Scotland a fortnight prior.

Rugby.title: South Africa suffer double injury blow ahead of Spain fixture
Rugby.summary: South Africa will be without all-time leading points scorer Libbie Janse van Rensburg for their WXV Global Series crossover fixture in Seville next weekend.
Rugby.body:
South Africa will be without all-time leading points scorer Libbie Janse van Rensburg for their WXV Global Series crossover fixture in Seville next weekend. The Springbok Women playmaker has returned home with an ankle injury sustained in her team’s 41-29 victory over Italy on Saturday.

To replace Janse van Rensburg, co-head coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September have called Mary Zulu into camp. Zulu, 23, has not won a Test cap since the Rugby Africa Women’s Cup triumph earlier this year. She did, however, captain a South Africa A team on a two-match tour of Brazil last month. In 18 Test appearances, Zulu has scored 45 points.

Rugby.body:
Saracens overcame a second-half red card for Nick Isiekwe to begin the Brendan Venter era with a seesaw 40-38 win at Leicester Tigers. Two tries from wing Rotimi Segun with Sarries short-handed saw the visitors prevail in a breathless 12-try affair at Welford Road.

Gabriel Hamer-Webb scored a hat-trick for Leicester, but it was to no avail as Venter's second stint in charge at Saracens got away to the perfect start. Venter's colourful first spell in charge brought a series of disciplinary run-ins, but set the foundations for the success that followed under Mark McCall.

Rugby.body:
Ireland held on to a 31-24 victory over Japan in the WXV Global Series at Dexcom Stadium in Galway. Two tries each from player of the match Brittany Hogan and Ireland’s new all-time women’s try scorer Béibhinn Parsons, as well as a score from Aoife Dalton, saw Scott Bemand’s side bounce back from their 40-36 defeat by the USA Women’s Eagles last week.

The Sakura Fifteen fought hard and dotted down for four tries, with Moe Nagaoka crashing over twice, Nijiho Nagata registered her team’s third from a maul and 18-year-old Nami Asari got over the whitewash in the closing stages.

Rugby.title: Talking points: 'Patchy' Ireland found a way to beat Japan in Galway
Rugby.summary: Ireland returned to winning ways in the WXV Global Series, rebounding from last week’s defeat to the USA Women's Eagles in Dublin with a 31-24 victory over Japan in Galway.
Rugby.body:
Ireland returned to winning ways in the WXV Global Series, rebounding from last week’s defeat to the USA Women’s Eagles in Dublin with a 31-24 victory over Japan in Galway. With the wind a prominent factor throughout, Ireland played with the breeze in the first half and opened up 19-5 half-time lead.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, Japan worked back into the contest after the break, scoring three second half tries when playing with the elements. However, Aoife Dalton and Ireland’s new record try-scorer Béibhinn Parsons crossed at crucial times, capitalising on Sakura Fifteen errors to ensure the hosts had enough to withstand the comeback.

Rugby.title: Why latest defeat feels different for Wales
Rugby.summary: Wales may have suffered another Test defeat, but Sean Lynn's new-look side has given fans plenty to be optimistic about before next month's trip to Japan.
Rugby.body:
It was another defeat for Wales, but this one feels different. As many of the three thousand-plus fans exited Cardiff Arms Park after the USA claimed a 26-24 victory, I assume they did so with a sense of optimism rather than the doom and gloom that often surrounds Welsh rugby.

What head coach Sean Lynn and his backroom staff have done to this group in just six weeks of pre-season is to be applauded. Wales have been transformed from a side which whimpered out of a winless World Cup and Six Nations into a competitive 80-minute team and one the nation can truly get behind.

Rugby.title: Rassie Erasmus had a few words for the officials amid Perth chaos
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus refused to reach for excuses or a gruelling Rugby Championship schedule after South Africa's dramatic 42-38 defeat to Australia in Perth.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus refused to reach for excuses or a gruelling Rugby Championship schedule after South Africa’s dramatic 42-38 defeat to Australia in Perth. Despite the match being repeatedly disrupted by reviews, communication problems and a remarkable period where the Wallabies were reduced to just 11 men by referee Andrea Piardi, the Springbok boss insisted the result came down to his side’s own shortcomings.

Erasmus admitted South Africa had “rolled the dice” with an experimental selection and accepted Australia were the better team on the night, while also going out of his way to praise Piardi and his team of officials for managing a chaotic contest under difficult circumstances.
Rugby.copy:
Rassie Erasmus refused to reach for excuses or a gruelling Rugby Championship schedule after South Africa’s dramatic 42-38 defeat to Australia in Perth. Despite the match being repeatedly disrupted by reviews, communication problems and a remarkable period where the Wallabies were reduced to just 11 men by referee Andrea Piardi, the Springbok boss insisted the result came down to his side’s own shortcomings.

Erasmus admitted South Africa had “rolled the dice” with an experimental selection and accepted Australia were the better team on the night, while also going out of his way to praise Piardi and his team of officials for managing a chaotic contest under difficult circumstances.

Rugby.title: Four men down
Rugby.summary: Australia are reduced to 11 men but dig in for a remarkable win against a much-changed South Africa side as they beat the world champions 42-38 in Perth.
Rugby.body:
Australia were reduced to 11 men but dug in for an extraordinary win against a much-changed South Africa side as they beat the world champions 42-38 in Perth. The Wallabies excelled with some vibrant attacking rugby, scoring five tries against the back-to-back World Cup winners to lead by 25 points with 16 minutes left.

But then a manic spell of four yellow cards in nine minutes left the hosts overrun, with South Africa mounting a comeback that ultimately fell just short. The visitors made 13 changes after beating New Zealand in Baltimore but still fielded a strong starting XV, which boasted 240 caps in the second row alone.

Rugby.title: Len Ikitau stars as 11-man Wallabies survive incredible Springboks fightback
Rugby.summary: Harry Potter and Fraser McReight's carries close to the line set up their fourth try, through the skipper, Harry Wilson.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss’ Wallabies have held on to beat the Springboks, 42-38, at Perth’s Optus Stadium on Sunday in an utterly captivating Test match. The Wallabies, who at one stage in the final ten minutes were down to eleven players, kept Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks out at the death to clinch an incredible victory over the back-to-back World Champions.

With the victory, the Wallabies clinched the Mandela Challenge Plate, continuing their unbeaten streak under Kiss in 2026. The 2025 John Eales medalist, Len Ikitau, was among the Wallabies’ best before succumbing to an ankle injury in the 53rd minute, crossing for a double in the first 40 minutes.

Tennis.title: Sabalenka stunned by Bartunkova at China Open
Tennis.summary: World number two Aryna Sabalenka follows Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she falls to a surprise defeat by Nikola Bartunkova.
Tennis.body:
World number two Aryna Sabalenka followed Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she fell to a surprise defeat by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova. It comes a day after top seed Rybakina, who defeated Sabalenka in last month's US Open final and replaced the Belarusian at the top of the rankings, was knocked out by Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva.

Czech Bartunkova sprung another upset at the WTA 1000 tournament and continued her breakthrough season with a 6-4 6-3 over Sabalenka. "I focused on myself, to be calm," said Bartunkova, who will face Austria's Sinja Kraus next.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu Is Going to Drop Outside The Top 100 And Yet Her Ranking Tells the Wrong Story
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu Is Going to Drop Outside The Top 100 And Yet Her Ranking Tells the Wrong Story Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
I have been pretty harsh on Emma Raducanu over the years. Some of it, I still think, was more than justified. After all, I was hardly the only voice criticizing her choices. The coaching turnover became ridiculous at times. Some scheduling decisions were impossible to understand. Too often a promising run would be followed by another absence or another reset or another explanation for why the momentum had disappeared.

Five years after winning the US Open, that remains her only professional singles title. There has also occasionally been a tendency around Raducanu to treat perfectly normal progress as evidence that another New York miracle might be just around the corner. It usually wasn't.

All combined WTA 1000 tournaments will award women and men equal prize money from 2027, the Women's Tennis Association said on Thursday, with the Italian Open and other major events joining the rest of the category in offering the same pay-outs.

In 2027 - nearly six decades after Billie Jean King won the Italian Open at the Foro Italico - the Rome clay-court event will finally award women the same amount of total prize money as men as part a "major milestone" initiative.

Tennis.body:
Men and women will receive equal prize money at all combined 1,000 events - the highest level of competition outside of the Grand Slams - from next year, the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) has announced.

Events at Indian Wells, California, Miami, Madrid and Beijing already met that commitment, as well as all four Grand Slams. However, the Italian Open, Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open will now also fall into line to meet a long-standing aim of the WTA, at events where men and women both feature.

Tennis.title: GB's Kartal wins on WTA return after six months out
Tennis.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal wins on her return to the WTA Tour after six months out with injury as she beats Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Sonay Kartal won on her return to the WTA Tour after almost six months out with injury as she beat Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open. The 24-year-old injured her lower back at Indian Wells in March and only made her return to tennis at the Billie Jean King Cup on 22 September.

Kartal, who narrowly lost to Czech world number 26 Marie Bouzkova on that return last week, produced a confident performance in Beijing to beat Spain's Lazaro Garcia 6-2 6-3. The Briton broke the qualifier's serve five times - helped by four double faults from her opponent - and landed 69% of her first serves.

Tennis.title: 'I kept fighting right to the end'
Tennis.summary: A tearful Kei Nishikori says he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ends his professional career at the Japan Open.
Tennis.body:
A tearful Kei Nishikori said he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ended his professional career at the Japan Open. Nishikori, known as one of the best players to never win a Grand Slam, lost 6-4 6-4 to world number eight Frances Tiafoe in Tokyo.

The 36-year-old became the first Japanese man to reach a major final when he faced Marin Cilic in the 2014 US Open showpiece. Nishikori beat then world number one Novak Djokovic on his way to the New York final and defeated Rafael Nadal for Olympic bronze at the 2016 Games in Rio.

Tennis.summary: American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" as she shares her long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.
Tennis.body:
American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" after opening up on long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.

Navarro, who claimed her first title in more than a year at the Strasbourg Open in May, is currently ranked 24th in the world. The 25-year-old was as high as eighth in 2024, the year she reached the quarter-finals at the Australian Open and Wimbledon, and the last four at the US Open in her native New York.

Tennis.title: Djokovic wins first match since Wimbledon in China
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic beats Nuno Borges at the China Open to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July.
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic maintained his remarkable unbeaten record at the China Open as he beat Nuno Borges to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July. The 39-year-old former world number one struggled in the second set but came through to win 6-3 7-6 (7-2) for his 30th consecutive victory in Beijing, albeit in his first appearance at the event since 2015.

Djokovic revealed in August that he has been dealing with an underlying health condition that causes particular issues in hot, humid conditions for "the past couple of years" and was far from his best against Portuguese Borges.

Tennis.title: Andy Murray Reveals Jack Draper Plans as Ranking Drop Creates New Concern
Tennis.summary: Andy Murray Reveals Jack Draper Plans as Ranking Drop Creates New Concern Yardbarker
Tennis.body:
When Andy Murray and Jack Draper joined forces this year, British tennis had huge expectations from the team-up. However, given Draper’s injury woes, it would have been understandable if there was speculation about Murray staying on as the coach, given the fickle nature of coaching partnerships in tennis. However, the former World No.1 had a very firm and practical answer when asked the question about his role in Draper’s team for 2027.

“Yeah, there’s still plans to help him,” Murray said in a Sky Sports interview. “I don’t know where that is. I’m not entirely sure because his ranking will have dropped. I don’t know if he would get into Australia, and potentially relying on wild cards and things like that, so we’ll see. “Hopefully he’ll be back on the court training again soon and getting ready for the new season – it has been an interesting year.”

Tennis.title: Zverev comeback leads Europe to Laver Cup victory
Tennis.summary: Alexander Zverev recovers from his day two defeat by Alex de Minaur to beat Learner Tien and clinch the Laver Cup title for Team Europe on the final day.
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev beat Learner Tien on the final day of the Laver Cup to lead Team Europe to their sixth title. US Open champion Zverev recovered from a disappointing defeat by Team World's Alex de Minaur on day two and eased to a 7-6 (7-3) 6-3 win over Tien at London's O2 Arena.

After Carlos Alcaraz's heroics kept Europe in contention after that loss on day two, Flavio Cobolli and Jakub Mensik beat De Minaur and Taylor Fritz in the doubles to extend their lead before Zverev's triumph.

Golf.title: The key move that boosts swing speed — and the tool that can help train it
Golf.summary: Learn how the Why Golf Power Plate can help you improve your weight shift, boost ball contact and create more power in your swing. The post The key move that boosts swing speed — and the tool that can help train it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you’re looking for more speed and better contact, the answer isn’t just to swing harder. A big part of the equation is learning how to move pressure through your feet and into your lead side before impact. When that sequence is right, it becomes easier to deliver the club with a stable lower body, find the center of the face and compress the ball instead of catching it fat or thin. That’s the idea behind Why Golf’s Power Plate.

The training aid sets your feet on a slight incline, giving you an exaggerated feel for a proper weight shift in your swing. First, the incline makes it easier to shift your weight back into your trail leg. Then the goal is simple: move that pressure into your lead side without letting your body slide away from the target.

Golf.title: 1 mental trick for playing consistent, high-level golf
Golf.summary: What's the key to playing consistent, high-level golf? On the latest Subpar, Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz shared their mental trick for staying even-keeled. The post 1 mental trick for playing consistent, high-level golf appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Both Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz know how difficult it is to play quality, high-level golf consistently and not let a bad shot, bad hole or bad tournament drag you down. Staying even-keeled and not riding an emotional roller coaster is often what separates good players from great ones, both in the professional and amateur ranks.

So, what’s the key to playing consistent, high-level golf? On the latest episode of GOLF’s Subpar Podcast, Knost and Stoltz answered a Subpar Hotline question from college coach Ethan Blair and shared one key mental trick they both use to stay even-keeled on the course. It all boils down to narrowing your focus.

Golf.title: Tom Kim's life-changing Asian Games win started with a message from Tiger Woods
Golf.summary: Tom Kim won gold at the Asian Games to earn an exemption from military service. His life-changing Saturday started with a message from Tiger. The post Tom Kim’s life-changing Asian Games win started with a message from Tiger Woods appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Tom Kim’s last PGA Tour win, which came at the co-sanctioned Genesis Scottish Open in July, ended with a congratulatory text from Tiger Woods. On Saturday, as Kim prepared for a career-altering round at the 2026 Asian Games, Woods sent him a different message.

“Just be you. Nothing more, nothing less,” the message from Woods said, via Korea’s Yonhap News Agency. Kim arrived in Japan for this week’s Asian Games under immense pressure. South Korean men between the ages of 18 and 35 are required to serve up to 21 months in the defense forces. PGA Tour pros Sangmoon Bae and Seung-yul Noh served during their prime and it impacted their golf. But the South Korean government awards exemptions to athletes who win a gold medal at the Asian Games or any of the three medals at the Olympics. Si Woo Kim and Sunjae Im won a gold medal in the team competition at the 2023 Asian Games, earning an exemption from military service.

Golf.summary: Former Masters champion Sergio Garcia is seeking to "terminate" his LIV contract in court, opening up pathways to other career opportunities. The post Sergio Garcia seeks LIV exit in court, eyes other Tour appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In the case of LIV Golf and its most famous players, a lot is yet to be determined. After the league filed for bankruptcy in September, it has been trying to earn commitments from players to join the new-look LIV 2.0 in 2027.

Golf.body:
Andrew Davidson does appreciate one view of his nickname. You don’t mind being called it in golf, because being it can be beautiful in golf. Basic pars are your friends. And a few years back, during one streak while at the University of Stirling, Davidson signed for them a lot.

He shot even par eight straight rounds, so of course his pals had to come up with something to call him other than “Andrew.” Thing is, though, it’s also a touch ironic. Most everything about the 32-year-old is decidedly un-bland. He is, in fact, accomplished at golf, and next week, he’ll be one of a dozen International players who will meet the American side at the Bridges Cup, a mid-amateur team event that’ll be played this year at Trump Turnberry, in Davidson’s home country of Scotland. Davidson’s list of golf achievements is long. He’s represented his country at the Home Internationals, the European Team Championship and the European Nations Cup. He’s won the Scottish order of merit. He’s a winner of the Welsh Amateur Stroke Play. He’s a winner of the Battle Trophy and East of Scotland Championship. He’s a two-time Scottish Area team champion.

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy Plan Relies On Player Equity Swap
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy Plan Relies On Player Equity Swap Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is filing for Chapter 11 protection after its Saudi backers cut off funding in April. The league owes millions in unpaid player salaries and legal fees. A new deal requires players to swap their unpaid cash for a majority ownership stake in the reorganized business. This move marks a desperate pivot from a cash-rich startup to a player-owned entity struggling to survive.

The financial math is stark. During the 90 days preceding bankruptcy, Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher received over $7.1 million from LIV Golf solely for legal fees. The firm agreed to discount its bills by 20% but still collected a massive sum. Meanwhile, the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, which spent over $5 billion trying to reshape pro golf, stopped writing checks. The league entered court with roughly $15 million in cash but faced a secured debt facility of approximately $495 million. That gap is too wide to bridge without a radical restructuring.

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s In-House Lawyers Remain as Gibson Dunn Discounts Fees
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s In-House Lawyers Remain as Gibson Dunn Discounts Fees Bloomberg Law News
Golf.body:
LIV Golf Inc. paid more than $7.1 million to Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher in discounted legal fees as the once Saudi Arabian-backed professional golf circuit was shedding much of its workforce, according to bankruptcy court records.

LIV began laying off most of its employees in August, but almost all its in-house legal staff, including chief legal officer John Ruzich, have agreed to remain with the business through October, said three sources familiar with LIV’s operations. The company’s agreement with private equity firm BC Partners Advisors LP, which is backing LIV’s move to restructure through the Chapter 11 process, would require that at least 50% of its players convert their unpaid compensation into a majority equity stake in the reorganized business.

Golf.title: From Pine Valley to Trump Turnberry, golf keeps taking Andrew Price places
Golf.summary: For Team USA Bridges Cup competitor Andrew Price, golf has taken him to places he only used to dream about. The post From Pine Valley to Trump Turnberry, golf keeps taking Andrew Price places appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
For Andrew Price, the best part of golf might not be the pars and birdies — it’s where the game takes him. Price, 44, grew up in Lake Forest, Ill., playing just about every sport he could. Basketball, baseball and golf among them. By the time he reached high school, though, it was clear golf was the sport that would take him furthest. After a successful junior career, Price played collegiately at Kansas, competing for a top-25 program and building friendships that have lasted a lifetime.

But the real journey was just beginning. After college, Price spent a couple of years in Arizona before returning home to Chicagoland, where he eventually settled back in the suburbs, joining his family’s fourth-generation insurance business, leaving him time on the side to get his game in shape for amateur events. What started with events like the Western Amateur and USGA qualifiers gradually opened doors to the highest levels of mid-amateur golf. And with each new opportunity came another unforgettable experience.

Golf.body:
Richard Bland says LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil has endured a "sad and difficult journey" over the past few months as he discussed the league's future. LIV Golf entered bankruptcy protection in early September, with at least $45m (£33m) reportedly owed to players.

The development came several months after reports that Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) would withdraw its multibillion-dollar financial backing of the tour at the end of the season.

Golf.title: He sold shirts at this year’s U.S. Open. Next year, he'll be playing in it
Golf.summary: Andrew Bailey, a sales manager for a golf-apparel company, won the U.S. Mid-Amateur on Thursday, earning a spot in the 2027 U.S. Open. The post He sold shirts at this year’s U.S. Open. Next year, he’ll be playing in it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Andrew Bailey, a 34-year-old sales manager at golf-apparel company Holderness & Bourne, didn’t have to be at the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills. He chose to be, volunteering his time to help out his brand in the hulking merchandise center.

Bailey also will be in attendance at next year’s U.S. Open at Pebble Beach — but in a markedly different capacity: as one of the 156 players in the field. Bailey’s rags- … well, quarter-zips-to-riches story became a reality Thursday when he won the 45th U.S. Mid-Amateur at Sand Valley Resort in Nekoosa, Wis., defeating Nate Smith, 5 and 4, in the 36-hole final.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia files to have LIV Golf contract terminated
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia files to have LIV Golf contract terminated RTE.ie
Golf.body:
Sergio Garcia is pursuing the termination of his LIV Golf contract, a potential path out of the league. As LIV Golf works toward fulfilling a restructuring agreement following Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, Garcia's attorney argued in a six-page courtfiling on Wednesday that termination "should not be objectionable" to the league because it "is consistent with (LIV Golf's) statement that the agreement is 'not part of (LIV Golf's) go-forward business plan.'"

The Spaniard's camp further argued that with the contract still in place, "tournament organisers, sponsors and other counterparties may hesitate before dealing with Garcia, who may be unable to represent that they are free of competing contractual commitments".

Golf.title: Is the U.S. Team overthinking their alternate shot pairings? | Subpar
Golf.summary: On this week's episode of Subpar, hosts Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz discuss what needs to change with the U.S. team's foursomes strategy. The post Is the U.S. Team overthinking their alternate shot pairings? | Subpar appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In the wake of the U.S. team’s thrilling comeback in Sunday singles to notch a 17-13 victory over the Internationals at the Presidents Cup, questions remain about the Americans’ performance in the team-match portion of the event — particularly in the foursomes format.

Foursomes — or alternate shot — has been difficult for the U.S. team in recent years. At this year’s Presidents Cup, the U.S. team went 2-7 in foursomes. And last year’s Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black was no better, with the U.S. going 2-6-0 against the Europeans.

Golf.title: Inside Apes Hill Barbados, a luxurious Top 100 golf resort in the tropics

Golf.body:
Here’s the truth about George Washington, the president who could not tell a lie: He left the country exactly once. That lone trip was to Barbados, where he spent six weeks in a house that bears his name today.

Washington was traveling with his half-brother Lawrence, who was seeking relief from tuberculosis. The island’s balmy climate was known as that: a balm. Rest and relaxation. Then, as now, Barbados is a fine place for R&R. It’s also become a great place for golf.

Golf.title: Is the bump-and-run *really* more reliable than a chip shot?
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Doug Spencer ran an experiment to find out if a bump-and-run is really more reliable than a chip shot. The post Is the bump-and-run *really* more reliable than a chip shot? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ditching high-loft wedges around the green in favor of a hybrid bump-and-run is one of golf’s classic pieces of advice, but do the numbers actually back it up? That was something I wondered recently, so I decided to conduct a small experiment.

We put three amateur players through a 30-shot test to see if putting with a hybrid produces better proximity and consistency than traditional wedge options. And not only did they test their mettle on both types of shots, when it came to the hybrid bump-and-run, this was their first time ever trying the shot.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia seeks exit from LIV Golf contract, while LIV Golf Australia venue says it hasn't been paid in court filings
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia seeks exit from LIV Golf contract, while LIV Golf Australia venue says it hasn't been paid in court filings Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Sergio Garcia is seeking official termination of his LIV Golf contract, according to new court filings. Last month, LIV Golf’s bankruptcy plea included a restructuring that would likely release LIV players from their existing contracts, allowing them to pursue opportunities elsewhere. Late Wednesday, Garcia’s lawyers and his LLC (Even Par) asserted they do not oppose this motion but do want clarification, as Garcia’s representation requests the court honor the request to end the agreement or allow Garcia to end it. As currently constructed, Garcia argues, the deal is confusing.

“So long as the Agreement remains of record, tournament organizers, sponsors, and other counterparties may hesitate before dealing with Garcia, who may be unable to represent that they are free of competing contractual commitments,” Garcia’s lawyers argue. “That uncertainty is particularly acute for a professional athlete, whose tournament schedule, sponsorship arrangements, and participation in other events must be planned well in advance, and whose competitive career is necessarily finite.”

Golf.title: Caolan Rafferty is Ireland's grand slam winner you don't know
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy won the career Grand Slam at Augusta in 2025. Six months later, amateur Caolan Rafferty became Ireland's other slam winner. The post Caolan Rafferty is Ireland’s grand slam winner you don’t know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In April of last year, Rory McIlroy crumpled to the ground at Augusta National, having finally won the Masters to complete the career Grand Slam. Six months later, the Isle of Ireland got another slam winner — one who has no equal. While McIlroy, who is from Northern Ireland, was the sixth member to join professional golf’s most prestigious club, Caolan Rafferty — who is from Dundalk, Ireland — is the only amateur ever to complete the “Provincial Slam” by winning the North, South, East, and West of Ireland championships.

The list of legendary Irish amateurs is long. The names include McIlroy, Shane Lowry, Darren Clarke, Padraig Harrington, J.B. Carr, John Burke and Hugh Foley, among others. And yet many of the biggest names didn’t have the extended amateur run that Rafferty has had, as they eventually turned to professional golf. Clarke and Foley won three of the four legs of the Provincial before turning pro. Lowry won two.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy confirms Abu Dhabi Championship return as Aldar named title partner
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy confirms Abu Dhabi Championship return as Aldar named title partner Golf Digest Middle East
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy will play the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links from November 5 to 8, the DP World Tour has confirmed. The announcement came alongside news that Aldar, the Abu Dhabi real estate developer that owns the course, has become title partner of the first of the season’s two Play-Off events. The tournament will now be known as the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

McIlroy arrives as six-time major champion, the reigning Masters champion and the defending Race to Dubai champion. He has never won in Abu Dhabi. “I’ve finished runner-up here four times, so I’d obviously love to go one better and finally win it,” he said. “I really enjoy finishing my season in the UAE, and hopefully I can have a strong week and put myself in a position to win another Race to Dubai title.”
Golf.copy:

Golf.body:
It was never about invitations to the fanciest clubs, the biggest sponsorships or the nicest cars. In fact, for a time it seemed he would be remembered most as a side-door entrant: someone who didn’t mind gritting his teeth and grinding out par against more talented players, despite a gap in raw ability that was evident even to him.

“In a nutshell… I have felt like I have done more with less than most,” John Peterson told GOLF.com Tuesday from his truck, en route to pick up supplies for his farm in Texas. “I think that’s probably what I’m most proud about when I look back on my golf career.”

Golf.title: This psychedelic golf retreat is a trip in more ways than one
Golf.summary: Guests stay five nights at a luxe seaside home in Los Cabos with an expert ayahuasca practitioner on site around the clock. The post This psychedelic golf retreat is a trip in more ways than one appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Golf courses are full of hazards, but the game itself isn’t dangerous. It’s not high-speed like auto racing or high-impact like the NFL. While you might tweak your back or jam a wrist, the risk of lasting harm is vanishingly low.

So why, when you play, are you so often afraid? Christopher Smith has long wrestled with the question. A GOLF Top 100 Teacher who has been an instructor for more than 35 years, Smith knows that sound mechanics can calm the heebie-jeebies (it’s not a bad idea to take a lesson!), and that mental strength can be a salve (nothing wrong with seeing a sports psychologist!). But he believes getting to the source of fear and discomfort sometimes requires going deeper.

Scotland's number one golfer, Robert MacIntyre, has called for Carnoustie and Muirfield to become regular venues again for the Open Championship. Carnoustie last hosted the tournament in 2018, when Italy's Francesco Molinari lifted the Claret Jug, while Muirfield's most recent staging was in 2013.

Next year's Open will be held at St Andrews and MacIntyre says more regular visits to Scotland would be a major boost for the game in the country. "That would be brilliant," he said. "I feel like there's not enough Open Championships in Scotland anymore.

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's endless quest has him frustrated after 'pretty shocking' week in France
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland hoped he was close to finding his old self, but one illuminating quote in France shows his endless quest continues to drag on. The post Viktor Hovland’s endless quest has him frustrated after ‘pretty shocking’ week in France appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Last month, Viktor Hovland’s PGA Tour season ended with a near-miss at the Tour Championship. It was a week that started with Hovland finding “something’ that allowed him to “hit the ball straight” to vault into contention at East Lake. Hovland was in position to win entering the final round but stalled, shooting 2-over as Scottie Scheffler caught and passed him to take the title.

Hovland has been in search mode for a while. He has won each of the past two seasons with the combination of a hot putter and a knack for competition, but that’s not what he’s looking for. He’s looking for something that is both familiar and foreign: who he used to be.

Golf.body:
For the average recreational golfer, the commonly cited odds of making a hole-in-one are approximately 12,500 to 1. For an albatross, or double eagle — a 2 on a par 5 — it’s approximately 6 million to 1.

Those odds are 1 in 14.5 quadrillion, according to one computation, which we’ll explain in a moment. In other words, virtually impossible. And yet — you guessed it — it happened.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: What's the maximum number of penalty strokes you can accrue on 1 shot?
Golf.summary: Is there a limit to the number of penalty strokes you can accrue by hitting a single tee shot? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: What’s the maximum number of penalty strokes you can accrue on 1 shot? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Hypothetical question: How many penalty strokes could a player get from hitting one tee shot? My thought: He’s late for his tee time, asks his opponent what club he used, tees it up in front of the marker, has too many clubs in his bag, uses an illegal club or ball, and then hits it out of bounds. Golf.title: Above Par: Precedent for LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy
Golf.summary: Above Par: Precedent for LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy wislawjournal.com
Golf.body:
LIV Golf New Jersey LLC filed for Chapter 11 protection on September 8, 2026, in the District of New Jersey. Five billion dollars in capital from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund funded five years of the tour before the money ran out. The rescue plan behind it comes with its own clock: BC Partners has agreed to anchor a $300 million recapitalization, but the restructuring support agreement gives LIV’s players 35 days from the petition date to sign on, or the deal is at risk. Player claims run to roughly $45 million, with Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau each owed more than $5 million of it.

None of this is unfamiliar to anyone who has spent time in sports bankruptcy dockets. We pulled fourteen professional sports cases filed over the last twenty years, from the New York Racing Association in 2006 to Grand Slam Track last December, and the range of outcomes across that set maps closely onto what LIV Golf is entering now.

Golf.title: How the Presidents Cup unraveled: 7 tipping points that cost the Internationals
Golf.summary: Something strange happened in the final seven singles matches at the Presidents Cup — and cost the Internationals the win. The post How the Presidents Cup unraveled: 7 tipping points that cost the Internationals appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Something strange happened with the final seven Presidents Cup singles matches on Sunday: They all made it to at least the 17th hole. Heck, five of those made it all the way to 18.

But even though the matches were close, the outcomes weren’t: The United States team won those matches 6.5 to 0.5. And so they won the Presidents Cup. “It was sort of on a knife’s edge for a long time there in the middle of the day,” said International captain Geoff Ogilvy just after the Cup was clinched. “You have a couple putts go in at the right time and the momentum goes our way, and it just didn’t do that today.”

Golf.title: Team USA escaped – but the Presidents Cup’s biggest flaw was exposed
Golf.summary: Team USA escaped – but the Presidents Cup’s biggest flaw was exposed Today's Golfer

The Internationals had Team USA broken and their own miracle at Medinah in reach. But their Sunday collapse exposed the flaw the Presidents Cup can no longer ignore. The United States simply reached the Presidents Cup’s Sunday singles, stopped trying to play as a team and remembered that, as individuals, they were much better golfers.

Brandt Snedeker’s side began the singles trailing 10.5-7.5. They finished as 17-13 winners after taking a record 9.5 points from the final 12 matches. The Internationals had entered the day five points from their first victory on American soil. They managed half of them.

Golf.title: Tom Kim left the Presidents Cup early — for very good reason
Golf.summary: Tom Kim won a Presidents Cup-leading four points. Then he raced to catch a flight: a gold medal and a military exemption is on the line. The post Tom Kim left the Presidents Cup early — for very good reason appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — It was a sad scene: A group of golfers, dressed in black, milling about in silence. Their caddies and families, standing beside them. And all watching as their red-shirted counterparts spilled onto the 18th green at Medinah Country Club, the United States team celebrating a win the International team had desperately wanted for themselves.

Golf.copy:

Golf.title: Think you want to be Team USA captain? Think again
Golf.summary: American Presidents Cup or Ryder Cup captains sign up for a whole bunch of stress. We saw that with Brandt Snedeker. The post Think you want to be Team USA captain? Think again appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Brandt Snedeker spent a sizable chunk of his Sunday evening pacing back and forth, back and forth between the 15th green and 16th tee. From afar, he looked steely, but up close, he was a frenzied mess of thoughts.

His phone was in and out of his pocket, one hand almost always covering his mouth, masking his words like a baseball pitcher does with his glove. He’d whisper softly into his radio set, then project more forcibly to his increasingly giddy American players, then back to a whisper for his assistant captains.

Golf.title: Grading every Presidents Cup performance from U.S. comeback at Medinah
Golf.summary: After another U.S. Presidents Cup win, let's grade every performance from a busy week for both sides at Medinah. The post Grading every Presidents Cup performance from U.S. comeback at Medinah appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In the end, the 2026 Presidents Cup was an exercise in extremes. And in the end, American dominance in singles play outweighed its ineptitude in alternate shot. After several stressful, underwhelming days from the home team reignited years-long debates about American match play preparation and team strategy, a 9-2-1 performance on Sunday at Medinah reminded us that, in the end, the best way to win at team golf competitions is to have the best players. If there was any doubt before the competition began in Chicago, there is no doubt now: the Americans are the more talented side.

Every year, team play competitions are an opportunity for the sport to take stock of itself. Is the American crop of talent as good as it looks on paper? Has the golden generation of International talent aged into a formidable threat to American dominance? Who are the young stars that will come to define the next decade of the event?

Golf.body:
Brandt Snedeker admitted to making “mistakes” as Team USA fell behind at the Presidents Cup at Medinah. With the Internationals taking a three-point lead into Sunday, there was no denying Snedeker’s claim that he had erred several times, including benching Scottie Scheffler in foursomes and a questionable pairing. The Americans’ leader had put them in a tough spot.

But when the dust settled on Sunday night after the Americans stormed back to win the Presidents Cup with a singles barrage, one thing was clear: Snedeker’s biggest decision likely won the Americans the Presidents Cup. It was a choice he made a month ago, but the payoff came at a critical juncture in Team USA’s historic comeback.

MEDINAH, Ill. — They could’ve celebrated and trophy-presented in one of the porta-potties for all Keegan Bradley could’ve cared. Golf.summary: The U.S. fought back admirably at the Presidents Cup. But at the Ryder Cup next year, the Americans can’t count on a Sunday down-three rally. The post U.S.’s uneven play at Presidents Cup won’t suffice at Ryder Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
On Sunday, the American team did what American teams always do when playing for cups of every size and shape, be it your Curtis Cup or Walker Cup, your Presidents Cup, your Solheim Cup, your Ryder Cup. Not always always, but pretty much always. Win or lose, when American golfers are playing their own ball in an 18-hole mano-a-mano match, they outplay their opponents.

In 1999, at the Ryder Cup at the Country Club near Boston, the Americans pulled out an unlikely victory with an 8.5-3.5 shellacking in the third and final act. Last year, at the Ryder Cup at Bethpage near New York, the Americans won another 8.5 points on Sunday, though that time it wasn’t enough to snatch victory from the mouth of defeat. On Sunday at Medinah at the Presidents Cup, the Americans won 9.5 points and the Internationals only 2.5 in a 17-13 American win.

Golf.title: US complete thrilling comeback to retain Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: The United States complete a thrilling comeback on the final day to beat the Internationals and win an 11th successive Presidents Cup.
Golf.body:
The United States completed a thrilling comeback on the final day to beat the Internationals and win an 11th successive Presidents Cup. The hosts, containing eight of the world's 11 top-ranked players, trailed by three points going into Sunday and were looking to avoid just a second defeat since the biennial competition began 32 years ago.

They dominated the singles, winning nine of the 12 matches, to seal a 17-13 win at Medinah - the scene of Team Europe's famous Ryder Cup comeback win in 2012. Jacob Bridgeman secured the decisive point by holing a four-foot par putt at the 18th to seal a one-up win over Australia's Min Woo Lee.

Golf.body:
U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker knows that no lead is safe around Medinah. Snedeker was on the U.S. Ryder Cup team that blew a 10-6 lead to the Europeans at the Chicago course in 2012.

So while Snedeker’s team entered Sunday at the 2026 Presidents Cup trailing the Internationals 10.5-7.5, he believed that things were far from over. That belief — in both his team and whatever Medinah mystique might exist — proved prophetic on Sunday as the Americans came out early in singles with a flurry of haymakers to grab the momentum and put the pressure on the underdog Internationals before polishing off a Sunday comeback, the biggest in Presidents Cup history.

Whatever happens on Sunday at Medinah, this year's Presidents Cup has unquestionably been a triumph that the event desperately needed. The International Team went into the singles with their first ever lead on American soil. The Internationals have certainly silenced those of us who had awarded the trophy to Team USA before a single shot had been hit this week. And with that, it is perhaps fair to say that this year's Presidents Cup has dealt yet another blow to LIV Golf by proving that those who made the jump are not needed.

Golf.title: What players and captains earn at the Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: At the Presidents Cup, performance has no bearing on payout, but the winning team walks off with a golden prize. The post What players and captains earn at the Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There was a time when playing for pride and country was enough. At its birth in 1994, the Presidents Cup paid its competitors exactly nothing. Every dollar the event generated went to charity. For 13 editions, from 1994 through 2021, no player, captain or vice captain received a cent personally. The Tour allocated money in their names to charities of their choosing instead.

That changed in 2022, when the PGA Tour introduced a $250,000 stipend for participants to use at their own discretion. The money is no longer earmarked for charity, though many players and captains still choose to give it all away. The Tour also continues to guarantee at least $1 million in charitable impact for the host city.

Golf.title: The next two Presidents Cups? Here's where they'll be held
Golf.summary: The next two editions of the Presidents Cup will bring the biennial competition to courses that have never staged the event. The post The next two Presidents Cups? Here’s where they’ll be held appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In the beginning, the Presidents Cup pressed repeat. For its first two editions, in 1994 and 1996, the Ryder Cup-style competition pitting the United States against the world (minus the UK, Ireland and continental Europe) was played at the same course: Robert Trent Jones Golf Club, in Gainesville, VA, a venue chosen largely for its proximity to the nation’s capital. The event, after all, was called the Presidents Cup, with Gerald Ford as its honorary chairman. It made sense to keep things close to Washington, D.C.

In those early goings, the PGA Tour, which created the event, had no plans to take it overseas at all. Not until it had gathered momentum — with the stirrings of a fan base and sponsor interest — did the competition settle into its current rhythm, shifting back and forth, every two years, between the U.S. and overseas (it was postponed in 2001 by the attacks of Sept. 11, and then again in 2020 by the pandemic). In 1998, the biennial battle moved to Australia; Royal Melbourne Golf Club was the stage.

Golf.body:
What do high-achieving pro athletes do to keep their competitive juices flowing after they’ve retired from their respective sports? Many take up golf, and some even showcase their skills on the celebrity pro-am circuit. But for a select few who desire even higher stakes, there’s the PRO Tour — an invitation-based tournament series created specifically for former pro athletes. The criteria for consideration: A player must have a minimum of two years of professional playing experience in their sport, a verified single-digit golf handicap, and a demonstrated commitment to preparation, professionalism, and competition.

Interested athletes can apply on the tour’s website to be considered to participate. In its inaugural season, the PRO Tour staged six regular-season events followed by two playoff events. Each event had a $500,000 purse. Top finishers in each event earn priority placement in subsequent events, while new additions to the tour are rotated in over the course of the season. The PRO Tour utilizes a modified Stableford scoring system, in which players earn positive or negative points on each hole based on their score. The player with the highest number of points over the course of the tournament wins.

Badminton.title: ‘It’s a Dream Coming True’
Badminton.summary: ‘It’s a Dream Coming True’ BWF
Badminton.body:
Egypt is on the cusp of making history, and Hadia Hosny couldn’t be happier. Cairo plays host to the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 – the biggest tournament ever held in the country. The three-time Olympian, former Member of the Egyptian Parliament, and now the President of the Egyptian Badminton Federation, talks of the significance of hosting the tournament:

What does it mean for you to have a tournament of this scale in Egypt? This is the first time ever we’re having a very big tournament like this. It means a lot. I was wishing this since I was an athlete and I feel like I’m the one on court right now (laughs).

Badminton.title: Suhandinata Cup Redraw: Korea Grouped With Denmark
Badminton.summary: Suhandinata Cup Redraw: Korea Grouped With Denmark BWF
Badminton.body:
Three-time champions Korea are grouped with European power Denmark at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 that will start in Cairo on Monday 5 October. The redraw for the World Junior Championships, necessitated by the withdrawals of Nigeria and Macau China after the original draw in August, was held today.

Korea, Denmark and debutants Cyprus are in Group H2, while Group H1 has second seeds Thailand, debutants Senegal, and Brazil. Defending champions China, the 5/8 seeds, are in Group E1 with South Africa and Zambia; Group E2 consists of Turkiye, Mauritius and Zimbabwe.

Badminton.title: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joshua Muguluma Richard
Badminton.summary: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joshua Muguluma Richard BWF
Badminton.body:
This is the 75th story in our Humans of Shuttle Time series, in which we present the perspectives of those who are involved with badminton at the grassroots level. Joshua Muguluma Richard, Shuttle Time Tutor with Uganda Badminton Association, talks of his journey in badminton.

I was born in Uganda, Kampala as the second of three boys. My childhood was shaped by simple living with strong family values and support from my parents. Growing up, I learned the importance of respect, hard work, and kindness from people around me. My social background was influenced a lot by the community I lived in, especially my neighbours who knew each other well and often helped one another during difficult times.

Badminton.title: A Course, a Coach, and a Winning Team
Badminton.summary: A Course, a Coach, and a Winning Team BWF
Badminton.body:
Among the participating coaches at the Shuttle Time Youth Leadership Workshop, being held in the runup to the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 in Cairo, was Dillan Schaap, who, earlier this week, had led his team to a significant triumph.

The All Africa Junior Team Championships 2026, which concluded on Thursday, saw South Africa edging Mauritius in a close semifinal before beating Algeria comfortably in the final. For Schaap, the win was vindication of the efficacy of the BWF Coach Education Level 3 Course that he had completed last year.

Badminton.title: World Juniors: Africa Beckons
Badminton.summary: World Juniors: Africa Beckons BWF
Badminton.body:
When the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships begin in Egypt on Monday 5 October, it will mark only the second time ever that the tournament has visited Africa. It has been 24 years since Pretoria in South Africa hosted the world’s premier junior tournament. With the 26th edition of the World Juniors, badminton in Africa is poised to make a big leap, entering new territory as it were. Participation from the continent is at a high – nine countries have entered.

Of the 47 teams competing at the BWF World Junior Team Championships for the Suhandinata Cup, 19 from Europe, 13 from Asia, four from Pan Am, and two from Oceania, besides nine from Africa.

Badminton.title: Asian Games: Vitidsarn, An Reign Supreme
Badminton.summary: Asian Games: Vitidsarn, An Reign Supreme BWF
Badminton.body:
Kunlavut Vitidsarn celebrated his return to the top of the world rankings by defeating Loh Kean Yew 21-12 21-16 for the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games gold medal on Tuesday. Both players had already made history by becoming their countries’ first men’s singles finalists. But Vitidsarn went one step further, denying Loh the rare feat of defeating two top-ranked players after the Singaporean had beaten Jonatan Christie in the quarterfinals.

“Really happy because I didn’t come here thinking about a medal. My (recent) performances haven’t been good enough,” admitted Vitidsarn. “Being world No.1 brings a lot of pressure because everyone thinks, ‘You are No. 1, how could you lose like this?’ It’s very difficult.”

Badminton.title: Asian Games: Indonesia Strike Twice, High for Loh
Badminton.summary: Asian Games: Indonesia Strike Twice, High for Loh BWF
Badminton.body:
Indonesia led a landmark day at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, with two of their doubles pairs toppling the leading seeds while a string of firsts emerged in the singles draws.

Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah produced an emphatic upset by dispatching top seeds Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping 21-12 21-14 to reach the mixed doubles final. The victory carried extra weight as the Indonesians were denied by the Chinese pair in a close World Championships semifinal in August, and had lost all five of their previous meetings.

Badminton.title: Why Property-Linked Investments Connect Financials Blackwall (ASX:BWF) and CVC (ASX:CVC) Beyond the S&P/ASX 200
Badminton.summary: Why Property-Linked Investments Connect Financials Blackwall (ASX:BWF) and CVC (ASX:CVC) Beyond the S&P/ASX 200 kalkine.com.au
Badminton.body:
BlackWall (ASX:BWF) has no borrowings on its own balance sheet. CVC (ASX:CVC) ended June 2026 with A$224.8 million of them. Yet both companies make their money from the same underlying source: stakes in Australian property that they own alongside other investors rather than outright.

That shared model is what connects them. Neither is a real estate Investment trust, and both earn returns through investment stakes, but those returns depend on property values, rezoning, rents and asset sales. Looking at where each one's Leverage sits, and what it is trying to do next, shows how differently two small property-linked investors can be built.

Competitor News.title: Standard Chartered turns F1 strategy into a brand story
Competitor News.summary: Standard Chartered turns F1 strategy into a brand story ContentGrip
Competitor News.body:
Standard Chartered has moved its Formula 1 partnership from sponsorship asset to brand story. Its new global campaign, "Move Ahead", does not focus only on speed, cars or race-day spectacle. Instead, the bank uses the preparation behind Formula 1 as a metaphor for how clients make decisions, manage risk and move across markets.

That distinction matters for marketers. Sports sponsorships often stop at access, logos and hospitality. Standard Chartered is trying to turn the behavior of the sport itself into a way to explain what the brand does.
